definitions.gloss: act of retaliation; retaliatory action; reprisal
definitions.explanation: An action taken in revenge or response to a prior hostile act. Used in international relations, workplace contexts, and general discussion of vengeful behavior.

examples.japanese: {報復行為|ほうふくこうい}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{禁止|きんし}→禁止：02643_kinshi⟧⟦されている→する：00392_suru⟧。
{内部告発者|ないぶこくはつしゃ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{対|たい}する→対する：02126_taisuru⟧{報復行為|ほうふくこうい}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{法律|ほうりつ}→法律：01722_houritsu⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{禁|きん}じられている→禁ずる：19600_kinzuru⟧。
examples.english: Retaliatory actions against whistleblowers are prohibited by law.

examples.japanese: ⟦{両国|りょうこく}→両国：10010_ryoukoku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{間|あいだ}→間：00914_aida⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{報復行為|ほうふくこうい}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦エスカレート→エスカレート：10727_esukareeto⟧し、⟦{緊張|きんちょう}→緊張：02494_kinchou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{高|たか}まった→高まる：02066_takamaru⟧。
examples.english: Retaliatory actions escalated between the two countries, and tensions rose.

notes:
A compound of ⟦{報復|ほうふく}→報復：14794_houfuku⟧ (retaliation, reprisal) and ⟦{行為|こうい}→行為：10021_koui⟧ (act, conduct). A formal term used in legal, diplomatic, and journalistic contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {報復行為|ほうふくこうい}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{出|で}る→出る：00513_deru⟧ — to resort to retaliation
- {報復行為|ほうふくこうい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{行|おこな}う→行う：01238_okonau⟧ — to carry out retaliatory action
- {報復行為|ほうふくこうい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{禁|きん}じる→禁じる：13737_kinjiru⟧ — to prohibit retaliation
- {報復行為|ほうふくこうい}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧みなす — to regard as an act of retaliation

DOMAIN USAGE:
- International relations: retaliatory sanctions, military reprisals between nations
- Workplace: retaliation against employees who report misconduct or file complaints
- Law: actions taken in revenge that may constitute additional offenses

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{報復|ほうふく}→報復：14794_houfuku⟧ — retaliation, reprisal (the concept without specifying an act)
- ⟦{仕返|しかえ}し→仕返し：10597_shikaeshi⟧ — getting even, payback (more colloquial)
- ⟦{復讐|ふくしゅう}→復讐：12512_fukushuu⟧ — revenge (personal and emotional, often literary)
- ⟦{制裁|せいさい}→制裁：11846_seisai⟧ — sanctions; disciplinary action (can overlap with retaliation in diplomatic contexts)
